title: Just-in-Time Entitlement Tokens and Audit Export Playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working playbook proposes a Just-in-Time (JIT) entitlement token design for RBAC v2 plus a compact, signed audit export format suitable for SIEM ingestion and long-term compliance proof. It focuses on minimizing standing privileges, providing verifiable evidence for every access decision, and enabling automated evidence packaging to feed our SIEM and archival store.

Context / motivation:
- Existing RBAC surface has many long-lived grants and an explosion of static entitlements that create audit noise and risk.
- Compliance teams want concise, tamper-evident packets of evidence tied to each access decision for retention and forensics.
- Operational teams need a low-latency path for ephemeral access that doesn’t increase token-store load or audit duplication.

Core concepts introduced here:
1) JIT Entitlement Token (JET): a short-lived signed token issued by the authorization service representing a decision for a specific principal-action-resource triple plus policy path and evidence references. TTLs are intentionally short (default 30s–5m) with configurable max 1h for scripted automation.
2) Decision Proof Bundle (DPB): compact signed JSON describing the authorization decision, inputs (attributes, policy version, cached assertions), and pointers to raw evidence (logs, attestation blobs). DPBs are the unit we export to SIEM and the archive.
3) Evidence Automation Worker (EAW): background service that collects required artifacts referenced by DPBs, normalizes/enriches them, and pushes either full bundles (for retention) or compact indexes (for SIEM) depending on sampling and retention policy.

Design details
- Token structure (JET):
  - header: {alg, typ, kId}  (alg = ED25519 / RSA; kId = signing key id)
  - payload fields:
    - subject_id (principal)
    - principal_type (user/service-account/role)
    - action (canonical action string e.g. inference:invoke:startSession)
    - resource (canonical resource id)
    - exp (epoch seconds)
    - iat (epoch seconds)
    - decision_id (uuid)  -- links into DPB
    - policy_version (string)
    - bound_context_hash (hash of request context: ip, region, route)
  - signature: server-side sign with rotating KMS key (HSM where required)

- Decision Proof Bundle (DPB) schema (compact example):
  {
    "decision_id": "uuid-...",
    "subject_id": "u-123",
    "action": "inference:generate",
    "resource": "model:mistral-7b:prod",
    "policy_version": "rbacv2-2025-02-10",
    "decision": "allow",
    "timestamp": "2025-03-10T16:22:18Z",
    "inputs_summary": {
      "attributes": "hash-abc123",
      "cached_assertions": "hash-def456"
    },
    "evidence_pointers": [
      "s3://evidence-buckets/proofs/2025-03-10/decision-uuid-... .gz",
      "kafka://audit-stream/decisions/topic/partition-3/offset-9821"
    ],
    "signed_by": "k-id-7",
    "signature": "BASE64SIG"
  }

  Note: DPBs stored in the fast index are intentionally small; raw evidence is stored separately and only linked. DPBs are signed so the SIEM/archival reader can verify provenance without fetching heavy blobs.

Evidence automation and sampling strategy:
- EAW collects raw artifacts referenced in DPBs and applies a tiered retention/sampling policy:
  - tier 1 (high-sensitivity): keep full raw evidence for 365 days (e.g., admin, key-management, private-deployments routes)
  - tier 2 (normal): keep normalized evidence for 90 days + compact DPB for 2 years
  - tier 3 (low-sensitivity / high-volume): keep aggregated counters + sampled full evidence (1%)
- Sampling must be deterministic per principal or per resource for reproducibility (use decision_id % N).
- EAW computes enrichment fields (geo-ip, service_tags, model_variant) and appends to DPB when pushed to SIEM to minimize downstream joins.

SIEM export contract:
- Two export flavors: real-time stream (Kafka topic: siem.rbac.decisions) and bulk daily export (ndjson.gz). Consumers must support verifying DPB signatures.
- Real-time record = DPB plus minimal enrichment. Bulk export = DPB + link to evidence bundles in cold store.
- Mapping guidance for common SIEM fields (recommended):
  - event.time = DPB.timestamp
  - user.id = DPB.subject_id
  - action = DPB.action
  - outcome = DPB.decision
  - resource = DPB.resource
  - policy.id = DPB.policy_version
  - evidence_ref = DPB.evidence_pointers[0] (primary)
  - proof.sig = DPB.signature

AuthZ service behaviors and caches:
- JETs are intended for short-lived local use (edge caches / runtime). The authz service retains a 7-day index of decision_id -> DPB for quick retrieval; raw evidence is held by EAW.
- If a route requires super-low latency and policies allow, we recommend local key-verified JET validation rather than an RPC to authz service. Validation verifies signature + bound_context_hash + exp.

Operational migration and rollout plan (proposed phases):
Phase 0: prototype + internal canary (4 weeks)
  - implement JET issuance endpoint and DPB canonicalizer in a feature branch
  - instrument two low-risk internal routes (dev-console and metrics-service)
  - enable local token validation in 1% of traffic
  - run EAW in dev cluster with full retention to tune cost
Phase 1: expanded canary (6 weeks)
  - onboard customer-facing non-PHI routes (hosted API inference read-only or test models)
  - enable real-time SIEM export for these routes only; validate DPB signing and SIEM verification scripts
  - run sampling policy to 5% for high-volume flows
Phase 2: staged rollout (8–12 weeks)
  - switch default issuance to JET for all hosted-api routes; allow config to fall back to legacy tokens per service until deprecation date
  - enable tiering rules with product teams to classify routes into retention tiers
  - integrate EAW with archive and SIEM ingestion pipelines
Phase 3: enterprise/private enablement + default enforcement (12 weeks)
  - add per-customer KMS key binding (enterprise private) for DPB signing if requested
  - tighten TTL defaults for privileged operations
  - finalize audit retention SLAs and export runbooks for compliance requests

Rollback and safety mechanisms:
- Fallback path: authz will continue to issue legacy bearer tokens for services that fail JET validation until they are patched.
- Circuit breaker: EAW can flip to compact-only mode if upstream storage costs spike.
- For forensic requests, preserve raw evidence retrieval API with access-controlled endpoints and an approval workflow logged to DPB.

Key management and signing considerations:
- Use KMS with hardware-backed keys for production DPB signing. Stagger key rotations monthly with overlap window.
- Keep signing key metadata (kId) in DPB and rotate keys with re-sign policy for archival bundles where required by compliance.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- Metrics to track: JET issuance rate, validation failure rate, DPB generation latency, EAW ingestion lag, SIEM consumer verification failures, storage cost per GB/day.
- SLO examples: 99.9% DPB generation within 150ms of decision; EAW ingestion lag < 30s for real-time route.

Checklist for teams to onboard:
- Add SDK hooks to request JETs for calls that currently use long-lived tokens
- Validate DPB signature and binding before trusting token-bound context
- Tag routes for retention tier and sensitivity (product owner input required)
- Provide mapping for SIEM fields if custom fields are required

Open questions and risks (working):
- How to best represent policy deltas inside DPB without making it large? (we currently store policy_version; diffs might be stored separately)
- Cost implications of keeping raw evidence for high-volume generative routes (embedding + token-level logs)
- Integrations with external customer SIEMs that require different field mappings and slower ingestion windows

Appendix A: example DPB (ndjson single-line)
{
  "decision_id":"d1c0e6b4-7a3e-4b2a-a7e9-2c6e5f9b8931",
  "subject_id":"u-2201",
  "action":"inference:chat:sendMessage",
  "resource":"deployment:redwood/llm-prod-1",
  "policy_version":"rbacv2-2025-02-10",
  "decision":"allow",
  "timestamp":"2025-03-10T16:22:18Z",
  "inputs_summary":{"attributes":"sha256:ab12...","cached_assertions":"sha256:cd34..."},
  "evidence_pointers":["s3://evidence/proofs/2025-03-10/d1c0e6b4.gz"],
  "signed_by":"kms:k1",
  "signature":"MEUCIQDh..."
}

Appendix B: minimal dev checklist for implementers
- generate test keys and verify signature verification workflow
- add bound_context_hash computation in request middleware
- wire EAW to local dev storage and confirm enrichment fields
- create SIEM consumer test harness that verifies DPB signature and fields

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: DPB size must be small for fast SIEM search and the raw evidence should be detachable. Feedback welcome on retention tiers and TTL defaults.
- Requesting review from product-hosted-api, eng-serving-runtime, and legal-compliance teams for policy versioning and retention limits.

-- Asha
